properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 27 at 3:39PM MDT until October 27 at 4:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
SVRABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
East Central Lincoln County in central New Mexico...
Northwestern Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico...

* Until 415 PM MDT.

* At 339 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 13 miles east of
Arabela, or 27 miles northwest of Roswell, moving east at 5 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of East Central Lincoln and Northwestern Chaves
Counties.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Heavy rains from severe thunderstorms can produce sudden and
dangerous flows in arroyos, ditches and over low water crossings. Do
not attempt to drive through areas where water covers the roadway.

The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS
EVENING TO 10 AM EDT WEDNESDAY.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to avoid or limit
outdoor exposure to wildfire smoke, reduce or avoid exertion or heavy
work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as much as possible.


For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 27 at 6:19AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Between 4 and 7 inches of heavy, wet, snow fell across the
Fairbanks Metro Area Monday. Warming temperatures Monday evening
have caused portions of that snowfall to melt creating many slushy
areas of melting snow and pooling water. Overnight low
temperatures Tuesday night into Wednesday morning are expected to
fall into the upper teens to low 20s which will allow much of this
slush to refreeze. Slick surfaces are very likely Wednesday
morning as wet surfaces and small water puddles freeze. Areas of
heavy, wet snow will also refreeze giving the slush a sturdier,
more ice like texture. Travel may be impacted, especially during
the Wednesday morning commute.

Additional rain and snow showers are expected overnight Wednesday
into Thursday with much lighter accumulations than Monday. Less
than an inch of new snow is possible with only a few hundredths of
an inch of liquid equivalent expected.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 27 at 5:41AM PDT until October 30 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 2.1 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at
12:15 PM Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at
12:56 PM Wednesday 10/28, 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at
01:43 PM Thursday 10/29, and 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW)
at 02:39 PM Friday 10/30. These predictions include up to 1.2
ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

in culverts and other stream passage structures to restrict flow

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM CDT
Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 7 AM CDT this
morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
